update.reference: Key priorities of the future state
update.quote:
End-to-End Process Automation with Minimal Manual Intervention

- Automated, AI-powered data pipelines—from acquisition to dissemination— reduce manual effort, increase speed and quality, and enable real-time responsiveness across all stages of the statistical business process.

- Employee input focuses on higher value work, innovation, and interpretation, not execution.
update.phase distribution reasoning: The intent is for automation and AI to touch every stage of the GSBPM—requiring every phase and sub-process description to reflect the idea that automation/AI where feasible can take over repetitive, routine, or rules-driven tasks, reducing manual intervention and freeing employees to focus on exceptions, analysis, and value-add work.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicit reference to automation and AI-powered pipelines from acquisition to dissemination implicates every GSBPM phase and sub-phase, as the text highlights end-to-end process impact.
implicated phases and subphases.description: All GSBPM phases and sub-phases each handle a specific domain in the lifecycle of statistical production (from needs specification to evaluation).
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Each phase and sub-process should explicitly acknowledge that automation and AI are embedded to shift manual and routine tasks to automated systems. The description should note that employee focus should shift toward innovation, interpretation, and oversight of automated systems, and that efficiency, quality, and responsiveness are improved by real-time, end-to-end AI-powered pipelines.

update.reference: Key priorities of the future state
update.quote:
Surveys as a last resort, not first response

- Exploiting existing data holdings is the first response for new/existing data needs. Admin data and alternative data is the second response for new/existing data needs. Surveys are only used if necessary and are optimized dynamically based on cost-benefit

- Designing, rendering and fielding a questionnaire is done using AI and takes no more than X time
update.phase distribution reasoning: Updates should apply to processes and decision points in the GSBPM that govern data sourcing strategy, data availability assessment, and survey design/implementation. These steps must emphasize a clear prioritization: use of existing and administrative/alternative sources before considering surveys, and when surveys are required, AI-driven rapid questionnaire production.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Using existing data sources and administrative/alternative data before resorting to surveys impacts needs specification, data availability checks, collection design, and survey sample design.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Checks whether current sources of data could meet user requirements and the conditions under which they would be available, including any restrictions on their use.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: This description should explicitly state that the first step is to exhaust the potential of existing data holdings, followed by administrative and alternative data sources, resorting to surveys only when those cannot meet requirements.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: AI-driven questionnaire design and dynamic optimization impacts the tools for collection, affecting collection instrument design and implementation.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Prepares a collection strategy for the data and determines the most appropriate collection instruments and methods.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Update to reflect adoption of AI methods for the design, rendering, and fielding of questionnaires, explicitly targeting substantial reductions in time and manual effort. The process should enable dynamic optimization based on cost-benefit analysis.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Survey minimization and dynamic fielding impacts how samples are selected and frames are created.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Applies to processes which involve data collection based on sampling, such as through statistical surveys, but it may also apply to other types of data collection.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Description should emphasize sample/frame design as a last-resort step after exploring non-survey sources, with AI used to optimize and possibly minimize respondent burden.

update.reference: Key priorities of the future state
update.quote:
Searchable, Usable, Actionable Data Assets

- All data and metadata are standardized, richly described, and machine-actionable—built for interoperability and reuse across tools, systems, and organizations.

- Discovery, understanding, and use are seamless for all types of users—whether human or machine—through APIs, metadata tagging, and open formats.
update.phase distribution reasoning: The update should infuse any phase or sub-phase that designs, prepares, or populates metadata—emphasizing enforceable, rich, standardized, interoperable metadata and open formats enabling both human and machine usability across processes. Dissemination/output integration is strongly implicated.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Standardization spans from data design through processing, analysis, and especially dissemination to guarantee machine-actionable and interoperable assets.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Defines the variables to be collected via the collection instrument, as well as any other variables derived from them. Preparation of metadata for collected and derived variables, statistical and geospatial classification is a necessary precondition for subsequent phases.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Include requirements for standardized, interoperable, and machine-readable variables and metadata. Should explicitly direct that variables be described and tagged for use in APIs and automated downstream processes.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Standardized metadata and discoverability concerns are fundamental in dissemination steps and post-processing.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Manages the update of systems (e.g. databases) where data and metadata are stored ready for dissemination purposes. Includes formatting data and metadata, loading them, and ensuring linkage to relevant metadata.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Specify that output systems must enforce machine-actionable, API-enabled metadata standards for all products. Dissemination data must be discoverable and usable seamlessly by both human and machine clients.

update.reference: GSBPM Roadmap Data In – Action Plan
update.quote:
Clear delineation sponsor (subject matter) roles and accountabilities, based on the minimum requirement that sponsors / subject matter are responsible for specification and certification (1.4, 1.5, 3.1, 4.4)

Full transfer of accountabilities for activities and functions related to data acquisition and collection to suppliers

Elimination of ‘dual accountabilities’ which can lead to disincentives to speed and statistical rigour
update.phase distribution reasoning: Updates should revise relevant process points to clarify sole ownership and accountability of each principal group—subject matter experts have responsibility for requirements/specification/certification; suppliers carry responsibility for operation/acquisition. Eliminate overlap.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicit mention of specifications and certification relates to concept identification and data suitability.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Clarifies the required concepts to be measured from the point of view of the users.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Include a clause specifying that the subject matter sponsor (not others) is accountable for defining and certifying the conceptual specifications.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicitly identified in quote for certification and data availability checking.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Checks whether current sources of data could meet user requirements and the conditions under which they would be available.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Stipulate that subject matter is responsible for certifying data requirements have been sufficiently checked and justified, with clear accountability for sign-off.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicitly named regarding collection instrument building.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Describes the activities to build and reuse the collection instruments needed during the Collect phase.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Description should indicate responsibility for instrument specification and acceptance is singularly assigned—typically, subject matter for specification, supplier for operationalization.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicitly named regarding finalising collection.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Includes loading the collected data and metadata into a suitable electronic environment for further processing.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Specify sole accountability for final data acceptance and certification—subject matter signs off on completeness/fitness, operational suppliers execute actual data handover and archiving.

update.reference: GSBPM Roadmap Data In – Action Plan
update.quote: Creation of a “centre of expertise” which works with subject matter specialists to expedite the negotiation and acquisition of administrative and alternative data
update.phase distribution reasoning: This update applies to the data suitability and acquisition phase, requiring the sub-process to explicitly mention or facilitate rapid, expert, cross-functional negotiation for external/alternative data sources rather than generic, slow, or ad-hoc practices.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Negotiating and acquiring alternative data sources directly addresses suitability and availability of external/administrative data.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Checks whether current sources of data could meet user requirements and the conditions under which they would be available.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Add that the phase should leverage a dedicated center of expertise to lead and expedite negotiations and acquisition of external, administrative, and alternative data in collaboration with subject matter specialists.

update.reference: GSBPM Roadmap Data In – Action Plan
update.quote: Pilot projects to enable partners to clean data using AI, prior to its ingestion by Statistics Canada (e.g. Cancer Registry) (2.4)
update.phase distribution reasoning: Update should be applied to the frame and sample design sub-process, making clear that data acquisition and pre-cleaning via AI (at partner site) is encouraged or preferred when working with external data.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Cleaning data with AI before ingestion impacts sampling frame design and sample creation, particularly where external data are used.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Identifies and specifies the population of interest, defines a sampling frame (and, where necessary, the register from which it is derived), and determines the most appropriate sampling criteria and methodology.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Include that, when practical, partners should be engaged to clean and standardize data using AI tools prior to data ingestion, improving downstream data quality and the integrity of the frame and sampling methodology.

update.reference: GSBPM Roadmap Data In – Action Plan
update.quote:
Assignment of full accountability for rendering to a single centre in Field 7 (3.1)

Design and implementation of questionnaire specification and rendering business processes which take advantage of AI (3.1)

Enforcement of pre-determined timeliness standards (for example, no more than x weeks between subject matter providing specifications and the start of collection) (3.1)

Reform of questionnaire building and prescription policies and directives (3.1)
update.phase distribution reasoning: All changes pertain to the design and construction of collection instruments. The process description should be updated to prioritize single-point accountability, AI-assisted questionnaire building, and enforceable timeliness standards, with clear, modernized policies.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: These are all direct changes to the collection instrument building process, as referenced by sub-phase id.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Describes the activities to build and reuse the collection instruments needed during the Collect phase.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Update to require that a single accountable group owns rendering; AI technology is to be utilized to streamline and expedite design and rendering; strict timelines from specification to launch must be enforced; policies must be kept current, reflecting AI and automation best practices.

update.reference: GSBPM Roadmap Data In – Action Plan
update.quote: Alignment of pre-collection (frame maintenance and sampling) and post-collection (processes and financial analysis) business processes and systems and ‘pipelines’ to facilitate maximum automation and minimize human interventions and programmatic patches (2.4)
update.phase distribution reasoning: The frame/sample design sub-process needs to highlight integration with automated pre- and post-collection workflows, aiming for seamless, hands-off, standardized data pipelines.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Focus on connecting and aligning frame and sampling with subsequent processes enhances automation between frame/sample design and later stages.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Identifies and specifies the population of interest, defines a sampling frame, determines sampling methodology.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Clarify that this sub-process is now designed to integrate automatically with upstream (pre-collection) and downstream (post-collection) business processes/systems to reduce manual interventions and allow for automated, end-to-end data pipelines.

update.reference: GSBPM Roadmap Data In – Action Plan
update.quote:
Modernisation of collection systems and platforms to include the use AI and other advanced methods to adjust collection efforts and re-assign cases in real time. (4.3)

Implementation of ‘one workforce’ model for collection (4.2 and 4.3)

Development and implementation into production of a range of sampling options, including person-based sampling (2.4)
update.phase distribution reasoning: Modern collection systems must support AI-driven, adaptive, and dynamic allocation of collection resources and methods. These updates also require explicit mention of flexible, customizable sampling strategies and an integrated workforce model.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicitly named as impacted for systems modernization and real-time adjustment.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Implements collection, manages contact with respondents, monitors and adjusts processes for data quality, closes and reports on collection.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Update to specify that advanced platform capabilities (including AI) should be used to dynamically optimize collection efforts, reassign cases, and maximize quality and efficiency in real time.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicitly named as impacted by new workforce and sampling models.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Ensures readiness and sets up people, processes and technology for data collection, including staff training.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Reflect that the 'one workforce' model is applied, supporting cross-training and flexibility so resources can dynamically shift to meet collection needs as determined by real-time AI recommendations.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Development of new sampling options implicates sample and frame design.
implicated phases and subphases.description: See prior.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Update to require that the sample/frame methodology accommodate multiple, flexible sampling approaches, including AI-guided person-based sampling and case prioritization.

update.reference: GSBPM Roadmap Data In – Action Plan
update.quote:
Investments in world leading collection research (4.4)

Implementation of experimentation mechanisms, including LFS Innovation Panel, to measure ‘what works’ (4.4)

Implementation of forums to foster a culture of constant improvement and statistical rigour (4.4)
update.phase distribution reasoning: Finalisation of collection should now be an iterative process, actively driven by research evidence, experimentation, pilot studies, and strong feedback loops fueling continuous improvement and quality assurance.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicitly named as being impacted (4.4) and relates to enhancing and finalizing collection using new research and experimentation mechanisms.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Includes loading the collected data, analysis of metadata and paradata, and archiving of collection materials.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Update to state that, at this stage, collection processes must be continuously informed by new research, ongoing experimentation, and evidence gathered through innovation forums and pilot panels—supporting a culture of improvement.

update.quote:
Expanded Digital Dissemination: Shift focus from static web publishing to dynamic, interactive, and API-driven platforms for more accessible and real-time data engagement.

Automation of Core Processes: Automate production and dissemination of data products (including data tables and PUMFs), improving speed, accuracy, and resource efficiency.

Metadata-First Approach: Implement comprehensive metadata standards and tagging, enabling external tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and other AI agents to accurately discover and extract relevant data.
update.phase distribution reasoning: Apply primarily to dissemination and output systems sub-processes—require all formal output products to be API-accessible, automation and metadata-enriched by design, so that dissemination is dynamic and discoverable by both humans and AI agents.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Focus on dissemination platforms and standards directly implicates output systems and dissemination steps.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Manages update and preparation of output systems for dissemination activity, including metadata.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Require that all data/metadata pushed to output systems is loaded, validated, and published in standardized, open, and machine-readable formats. Systems should expose data via APIs and comprehensive metadata tagging.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Automation of product production and dissemination implicates dissemination product creation and release.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Produces dissemination products (publications, tables, open data, etc.) as previously designed to meet user needs.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Specify that product creation is to be automated where feasible, and outputs must be structured for both human and automated/AI consumption, with all products supporting real-time, API-enabled access.

update.quote: Make PUMFs mandatory, use automated methods for creation of PUMFs
update.phase distribution reasoning: Apply to dissemination sub-process—require that PUMFs are always produced as standard deliverables, and that the process for doing so is automated to minimize burden.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Mandatory, automated production of microdata products affects how dissemination products are prepared for public use.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Produces dissemination products (publications, tables, open data, etc.) as previously designed to meet user needs.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Require that the production of PUMFs is standardized, automated, and forms a compulsory dissemination component for relevant datasets, ensuring timeliness and reducing manual effort.

update.quote:
Discuss the type of product to disseminate before it gets to the end of the GSBPM process.

Not all projects require a data visualization for example as users will do it themselves.
update.phase distribution reasoning: Apply upstream to dissemination and output design steps: require explicit, early decision-making about which dissemination products and value-add outputs (e.g., visualizations) are required or not, avoiding duplication and unnecessary effort.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Early discussion of dissemination products and need for data visualization ties dissemination design back to initial needs assessment and output definition.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Contains the detailed design of the statistical outputs, products and services to be produced, including dissemination.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Mandate that during this phase, dissemination product types and visualization requirements are explicitly reviewed and rationalized, with an option to exclude certain products when analysis suggests users can/will create them independently.

update.reference: Data and Information Governance and Stewardship Table
update.quote: Incorporate AI agents capable of interpreting data-sharing agreements, executing governance policies dynamically (e.g., privacy, retention, classification), and mediating context-aware access based on metadata, provenance, and purpose.
update.phase distribution reasoning: While this proposal overlays the whole lifecycle, descriptions of process, analyze, and disseminate phases should mention embedded, automated, AI-driven governance modules ensuring continuous, context-aware policy enforcement, dynamic data access, and compliance.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Governance overlays the entire statistical data lifecycle but specifically impacts data access, privacy, and compliance steps in process, analyze, and disseminate phases.
implicated phases and subphases.text: All Phases — Focus on Process, Analyse, Disseminate
implicated phases and subphases.description: Phases 5, 6, and 7 govern data transformation, value-add, and release steps.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Revise the phase descriptions to require AI/governance agents throughout, automating real-time policy enforcement and monitoring of privacy, retention, and access control, and ensuring actions for data use are authorized, logged, and compliant as data is processed, analyzed, and disseminated.

update.reference: Data and Information Governance and Stewardship Table
update.quote: Shift from active data collection to a passive model for collection
update.phase distribution reasoning: Impacts collection strategy and instrument sub-processes, which should explicitly prefer and accommodate passive ('byproduct') data acquisition from digital sources when feasible instead of relying solely on active solicitation.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Passive data collection fundamentally alters collection planning and execution components.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Prepares a collection strategy for the data and determines the most appropriate collection instruments and methods.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Update to include explicit provisions for designing collection via passive (e.g., digital traces, admin data flows) methods and ensuring instruments/systems are built for event- or system-based data capture, not just active collection.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Where passive models are implemented this redefines collection processes.
implicated phases and subphases.description: The different collection instruments are used to collect information, which may include raw microdata or aggregates produced at the source, as well as any associated metadata.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Highlight systems to enable passive data flow ingestion, with required validation, automation, and lower respondent burden, integrating event- or trigger-based automation over scheduled manual collection.

update.quote:
Ensure minimum metadata requirements are respected for every data collection/acquisition process
Use AI to enhance the extraction of structured data from unstructured sources
Ensure metadata to identify credible data sources to reduce mis/dis-information
Automate recurring data acquisitions with external partners
Use AI/ML to populate metadata repositories (fill gaps) and IM data tagging, at ingestion
update.phase distribution reasoning: Target sub-process stages of collection and acquisition to formalize minimum metadata standards, require AI-driven metadata enrichment/verification, automate routine acquisitions, and ensure credible data provenance is tracked at point-of-ingestion.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Each collection or acquisition process must meet minimum metadata and reliability requirements, implicating collection setup.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Ensures that people, processes, and technology are ready to collect data and metadata.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Expand to explicitly include validation of minimum metadata standards at setup, AI-assisted identification of source credibility, and automation setup for recurring acquisitions.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Automating acquisition and metadata enrichment at ingestion implicates run and finalize collection.
implicated phases and subphases.description: The collection is implemented and information gathered using the collection instruments.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Clarify that AI/ML should be leveraged at data ingestion to auto-tag or enrich metadata and validate credibility as part of the collection workflow.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Ensuring credibility and comprehensive metadata also implicates finalise stages.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Includes loading collected data and metadata into a suitable environment for further processing.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Update to reflect that closing a collection includes automated checks for metadata completeness, machine-actionable tagging, and automated provenance validation steps.

update.quote:
Expand use of SDMX throughout the data lifecycle process
Leverage .STAT tools for data processing & analysis
Amplify use of AI/ML to apply classification codes/standards
Prescribe the use of data management tools (Aria/Colectica)
update.phase distribution reasoning: Process, analysis, and variable design sub-processes should mandate the use of SDMX, .STAT, and prescribed tools for standardization and automated processing/classification, ensuring coherent, interoperable data structures and analysis-ready files.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicitly targets processing, analysis and standardization, involves SDMX, classification, and data management tool usage.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Classifies and codes the input data.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Mandate the use of SDMX and machine-assisted (.STAT/AI) tools for standardization, classification, and coding to increase consistency and reduce manual effort.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Tool usage for processing and analysis involves design and analytical phases.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Transforms raw or processed data into statistical outputs.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Explicitly require the adoption of prescribed toolsets and standards (e.g., SDMX, .STAT, Aria/Colectica) for the production, standardization, and automation of analytical outputs.

update.quote:
GSBPM 5 sub-processes are orchestrated in modular, event-driven frameworks that are automated and version-controlled by design. Analysts are no longer required to manually intervene, clean or manipulate files.

AI-enabled modules handle 50% of manual interventions for activities such as classification, edits and imputation for administrative and survey data.

Every processing pipeline is auditable, reproducible, and deployable across subject-matter domains. Meta-data driven and standardization are default by design.

Data processing turnaround time has reduced by 50% across survey programs through automation and orchestration.
update.phase distribution reasoning: Apply to all sub-processes of phase 5 (Process)—descriptions should emphasize event-driven, modular, automated orchestration, AI handling of standard interventions, comprehensive versioning and audit trails, and default metadata standardization.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Orchestration and automation of processing pipelines directly reference GSBPM 5 and all its sub-phases, especially classification, imputation, derivation, aggregation.
implicated phases and subphases.description: 8 sub-processes that integrate, classify, check, clean, and transform input data, preparing them for analysis/dissemination.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Each sub-process should be reframed to expect modular, version-controlled, (event-driven) automation as the primary implementation, with AI applied to standard interventions, human review focused on exceptions, and all actions/actions thoroughly logged for reproducibility.

update.quote: Emphasis on the need for the right people to handle technical aspects and the importance of standardizing data formats.
update.phase distribution reasoning: All variable design and data finalization sub-processes should explicitly mention standardized formats and the need for staff with up-to-date technical skills to design, verify, and implement these standards.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Standardizing data formats, while not explicitly referencing a single phase, affects design, processing, analysis and dissemination.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Defines the variables to be collected via the collection instrument and derived variables
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Emphasize standardization as essential and expect staff to possess, or be trained in, current data/metadata standards. Variables must be captured in formats that will remain consistent and interoperable throughout the production lifecycle.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Uniform formats for downstream use impact processing functions.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Brings together results in a data set, used as input for analysis or dissemination.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Update to require that final data be rendered in formally prescribed, standardized file and metadata formats ensuring compatibility, automation-readiness, and documentation.

update.quote:
Implement AI-supported pipelines for auto-generated descriptive and exploratory analysis including daily write-ups, dashboards, and standardized analytical products.

Build infrastructure and tooling that enable real-time analytical workflows with intelligent validation and anomaly detection.
update.phase distribution reasoning: Analytic sub-processes must be updated to adopt AI-driven, automated, and real-time tools for output/insight production and validation, supporting reduced lead times and fit-for-purpose outputs.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: AI-support for auto-generating outputs and dashboards directly impacts the drafting and interpretation steps within Analyse.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Transforms processed data into statistical outputs such as indexes, tables, maps, etc.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Specify that output drafting includes automated and AI-supported creation of standardized and customized analytical outputs, dashboards, and narrative write-ups.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Validation/anomaly detection targets output validation.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Validates outputs produced for quality, coherence, and compliance with standards.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Require the use of automated tools for real-time validation and anomaly/outlier detection, reserving human validation for issue investigation and sign-off.

update.quote:
GSBPM 8.1 (Gather evaluation feedback), LLMs can help collect and analyze both internal and external feedback from users, respondents, and stakeholders.

GSBPM 8.2 (Conduct evaluation), LLMs can assist in evaluating the overall performance of statistical processes by analyzing feedback data and suggesting potential improvements for the next iteration of a survey or process.
update.phase distribution reasoning: Evaluation sub-processes should explicitly mention LLMs/AI for automatic aggregation, analysis, and synthesis of feedback and suggestions, with human experts supplementing and acting on algorithm-generated recommendations.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicitly references GSBPM 8.1 and 8.2 and describes LLMs supporting gathering inputs and evaluation.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Gathers evaluation inputs from across phases, making them available for assessment.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Update to specify that the process can use LLMs to aggregate, cluster, and summarize feedback, facilitating comprehensive and timely input collection across user, respondent, and internal channels.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: References evaluation of performance and feedback analysis.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Synthesizes evaluation inputs into a report/dashboard, determining process success and improvement areas.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Description should include the use of AI/LLMs to analyze performance metrics, generate automated recommendations, and inform evaluation/continuous improvement cycles.

update.quote: GSBPM 7.2 (Produce Dissemination Products): LLMs automate the creation of dissemination products, generating draft reports, summaries, or narratives from data tables, which analysts can refine for specific audiences. AI also assists with automated charts and visual representations of data.
update.phase distribution reasoning: Apply to automated drafting/generation of dissemination outputs. Human review, refinement, and sign-off should be kept, but initial content should be AI/LLM-generated wherever possible.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicitly named (7.2), with LLMs supporting product creation.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Produces the dissemination products, as previously designed in sub-process 2.1, to meet user needs.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Specify that all draft reports, tables, and visual outputs should be machine-generated using LLMs/AI, with humans focusing on tailoring/reviewing content for their audiences and specific dissemination contexts.

update.quote: GSBPM 6.1 (Prepare Draft Outputs): LLMs streamline report generation by automating draft outputs (e.g., summaries, tables, charts), allowing analysts to focus on interpretation.
update.phase distribution reasoning: Apply to process for drafting outputs (analysis phase)—primarily, AI/LLMs to automate initial generation, with humans responsible for higher-level interpretation and context.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicitly referenced as target of update for report generation.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Transforms data into statistical outputs.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Description should note that initial drafts (summaries, tables, charts, etc.) are to be generated by LLMs/AI, freeing analysts for in-depth review and interpretive work.

update.quote: GSBPM 5.1 LLMs can automate record linkage across multiple datasets, reducing manual errors and ensuring a comprehensive, accurate integrated dataset for analysis.
update.phase distribution reasoning: Update data integration sub-process to explicitly prioritize LLM/AI/ML-driven tools for record linkage, reducing manual matching/intervention.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicitly referenced—record linkage falls under data integration.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Integrates data from one or more sources.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Update to specify that linking and harmonizing records from disparate datasets should be accomplished by AI/LLM methods (where feasible) to accelerate integration, reduce error, and improve comprehensiveness.

update.quote: GSBPM 4.1 (Create frame and select sample): LLMs can support record linkage to create a more accurate sampling frame.
update.phase distribution reasoning: Update the description and practices of frame/sample creation to endorse use of LLMs/AI for integrating, matching, and validating population frames.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicitly noted—LLMs used for frame/sample building and record linkage.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Establishes the frame and selects the sample for this iteration of collection.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Expand to require or recommend AI/LLM-powered record linkage for building accurate, up-to-date sampling frames from internal/external/multisource data.

update.quote: GSBPM 2.2 (Designing variable descriptions): LLMs can assist in generating and refining descriptions for statistical variables.
update.phase distribution reasoning: Apply to variable description design—explicitly note that AI/LLMs should be used to generate/standardize variable descriptions and metadata at design time.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicitly referenced as target—generating and refining variable descriptions.
implicated phases and subphases.description: Defines the variables to be collected via the collection instrument, as well as other variables that will be derived.
implicated phases and subphases.update application to description reason: Include that AI/LLMs are applied to generate, validate, and standardize variable names, definitions, and metadata, contributing to interoperability, clarity, and discoverability.
